title: Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald (Luftgau VII), Funksprüche in the Luftgauschlüssel double transposition, Western campaign 1940
correspondents: Flugabwehrkommando Schwarzwald and its Flak groups/regiments (Luftgaukommando VII, Munich) ↔ subordinate Flak units
place: Black Forest / Upper Rhine (Flak-Gruppe Schwarzwald-Süd and -Nord)
shelfmark: NARA RG 242, T405 (German Air Force Records of the Luftgaukommandos, Flak ...), roll 9 (NAID 332033680)
folio_note: c. 70 Funkspruch forms in five-letter groups, frames 863-867 (one message in 5 parts, 'Un 1.Tl-179' ... '5.Tl-204'), 889-901, 917-936, 947-948, 964-1003, 1010-1011, 1025-1056, 1069-1105, 1113 (plus 565, 9); most messages are multi-part ('1.Tl', '2.Tl' ...) of 160-250 letters. Frame 349: an exercise Fernschreiben of 25.2.1939 (221 letters) to Luftverteidigungskommando Berlin; frame 350: its key card 'Annahme: Luftgauschlüssel für den 25.2.1939', two transposition keys a (21) and b (19), Kenngruppen qli vzn fks puc.
status: Not on DECODE, not in the repo (known.py: T405, Schwarzwald, Luftgau: no hits). The letter counts of the groups are those of German plaintext with X as word separator (pooled IC 0.060 on noisy OCR, top letters E R X I N A), so this is a transposition, not Enigma. Tested 27 Oct 2026: the 1939 exercise message reads in full with its key card (double columnar transposition, key a then b, the group containing the Kenngruppe 'fks' at group 7 dropped, CH written Q): 'ROEM X ERSTE FLAKREGIMENT X ZWOELF X RES X FLAKABTEILUNG ... WERDEN IN DER NACHT DURQ TEILE DER X FLAKTRANSPORTABTEILUNG X DREIEINS X NAQ X MAGDEBURG X VERLEGT X LUFTGAUKOMMANDO X ROEM X DREI' (dw1939.py). The 1940 messages carry no key and no decipherment on the frames; some have a typed Fernschreiben in clear on a neighbouring frame (e.g. 862, 4 June 1940) that may be the same text.
why: A large, dated file of German hand-cipher (Doppelwürfel) radio traffic from 1940, with the system and one key proven from the same reel: a ready test bed for double-transposition hill-climbing and possibly cribbed by the clear Fernschreiben filed beside it.
score_note: Scored from NARA OCR during the Oct 2026 NARA bulk-scan triage (research/nara_triage_g/); frames 349-350 and the key verified on the images, the 1940 messages read from OCR only
verify: Transcribe the five-part message of frames 863-867 and two or three same-day messages from the images; match them to the clear Fernschreiben on neighbouring frames (862, 878, 888, 897 ...) as cribs; then run a double-transposition solver with key lengths 15-25 (one daily key per day for all messages).

title: British consular cipher telegrams (Vigo → Foreign Office 1939; Gibraltar ↔ British consul Las Palmas, Lisbon/Lagos → consul Tenerife 1940), copies obtained by the German naval attaché Madrid and sent to OKW/Chi
correspondents: British consul Vigo → Foreign Office London; British authorities Gibraltar, Lisbon, Lagos → British consuls Las Palmas and Tenerife
shelfmark: NARA RG 242, T1022 (Copies of Records of the German Navy), rolls 2865 (NAID 338541514) and 2866 (NAID 338542419); OKW Ausland IV files B.Nr. 1440/39 gKdos and 3022/40
folio_note: Roll 2865 frames 362-366: Marineattaché Madrid B.Nr. 128/39 g.Kdos (20.11.1939) 'Englische Konsularchiffer im Verkehr mit Auswärtigem Amt', copies of the Vigo consul's telegrams of 11-12.11.1939 (5-figure groups, some letter groups) on the sailing of eight German steamers; forwarded 1.12.1939 to W.F.A./Chi. (an earlier batch B.Nr. 97/39 of 21.10.1939 not located). Roll 2866 frames 503-515: Marineattaché Madrid B.Nr. 597 g (21.5.1940) 'Feindliche Schlüsseltelegramme', anonymous copies of April 1940 telegrams: 5-figure group telegrams Gibraltar → British Consul Las Palmas on Spanish telegraph forms (frames 504, 508-515), 'Nota num. 5-7' letter-group telegrams Lisbon/Lagos → British consul Tenerife (frame 507).
status: Not on DECODE, not in the repo. The covering letters submit the copies 'zwecks möglicher Auswertung'; no decipherment or Chi reply is filed with them on these frames. British consular traffic of 1939-40 was in hand book ciphers (figure codes with subtractor tables); the system is not identified here.
why: British reporting from neutral Spanish ports on German blockade-runners at the start of the war, intercepted by German agents; any reading would show what the consuls reported and whether German Chi read it.

title: French consular agent Las Palmas → Marine Casablanca, letter-cipher telegrams ('Nota num. 2-4') copied by an anonymous informant for the German naval attaché Madrid
correspondents: Agent consulaire de France, Las Palmas → Marine (French Navy) Casablanca
shelfmark: NARA RG 242, T1022 roll 2866 (NAID 338542419), frames 505-507 (OKW Ausland IV 3022/40)
folio_note: Three short telegrams in five-letter groups: 22.4.1940 (frame 505, c. 14 groups), 'Nota num. 3' 24.4.1940 (frame 506, c. 30 groups), 'Nota num. 4' 28.4.1940 (frame 507, c. 25 groups), each with the informant's German note.
status: Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Submitted to OKW Ausland IV for 'mögliche Auswertung'; no decipherment on the frames. French naval traffic of 1940 used code with letter superencipherment; system not identified.
why: French naval intelligence reporting from the Canaries in the last weeks before the German offensive in the West.

title: Kriegsmarine Etappendienst / OKW Abwehr IV 'Scheintelegramme' in the W.f.S. (Wörterbuch für Scheintelegramme 1930/1936: Hapag-Lloyd code + Kammwürfel transposition): radio telegrams to M.S. Havelland, Aug 1940, filed without clear text
correspondents: OKW Ausland IV / Etappe → German merchant ship M.S. 'Havelland' (Yokohama) via DEBEG ship radio
shelfmark: NARA RG 242, T1022 roll 3391 (NAID 338968820), frames 877-878; system and plain/cipher pairs on rolls 3391, 3367 (NAID 338928415) and 2864 (NAID 338540609)
folio_note: Roll 3391 frames 877 (3.8.1940, c. 160 groups, 'DGR-DZG DFB-DFQ') and 878 (1.8.1940, c. 35 groups): no Klartext on the frames. Key material in the same rolls: 3391 frames 614-617 (Jan 1940 proposal to change the W.f.S. procedure, with a worked example 'Englischer schwerer Kreuzer ...' in old and new form), 91 (telegram with code numbers glossed '0898 = unter Bezugnahme ...'); roll 3367 frames 221-230 (KALORLUX Hamburg telegrams Jan-Mar 1938 each with 'Klartext'); roll 2864 frame 837 (21.11.1938 telegram with Klartext).
status: Not on DECODE, not in the repo. The W.f.S. is a commercial-code (Hapag-Lloyd) dictionary with a columnar 'Kammwürfel' step; several telegrams in the same rolls are filed with their clear text, so the code list and the transposition can be rebuilt from pairs; the two 1940 radio telegrams have no clear text with them.
why: Abwehr/Etappe instructions to a blockade-running supply ship in Japan in 1940; and a documented German naval-agent hand system with plain/cipher pairs, not on DECODE.
